## Submitted Manuscripts

::: {.output-list .editorial-list}
::: {.output-item}
<p><span class="status-badge">Submitted Manuscript</span></p>
<h3>“全域-自我”视角下全球生物医药顶尖科学家城际流动网络结构与形成机制</h3>

Role: First author.

This manuscript connects whole-network structure with scientist-level mobility ego-networks to examine the formation of intercity mobility networks among elite biomedical scientists. It extends the accepted city-network article by placing city-level network position and individual embeddedness in the same analytical frame.
:::

::: {.output-item}
<p><span class="status-badge">Submitted Manuscript</span></p>
<h3>Pre-move coauthor ties and the direction of scientific mobility: A city-level choice analysis of highly cited biomedical scientists</h3>

Role: First author.

This manuscript treats observed intercity employment moves as event-specific destination choices. It compares selected cities with alternative candidate destinations and measures pre-move coauthor ties as prior relational exposure.
:::
:::

## Accepted Article

::: {.output-list .editorial-list}
::: {.output-item}
<p><span class="status-badge">Accepted</span></p>
<h3>城市网络视角下全球生物医药顶尖科学家流动的空间结构与影响因素</h3>

Role: First author. Accepted by *World Regional Studies*.

The article analyzes the spatial structure of elite biomedical scientist mobility from a city-network perspective and examines city-level factors associated with mobility-link formation.
:::

## Selected Research Outputs

::: {.output-list .editorial-list}
::: {.output-item}
<p><span class="status-badge">Research Manuscript</span></p>
<h3>Assessing Urban Resilience Using Nighttime Light Remote Sensing and Fisher Information</h3>

Role: First author.

This study uses VIIRS-DNB daily nighttime-light data, Fisher Information, dynamic time warping, and K-Means clustering to compare resilience trajectories across 48 cities in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei, Yangtze River Delta, and Pearl River Delta urban agglomerations during the COVID-19 shock.
:::

::: {.output-item}
<p><span class="status-badge">Research Manuscript</span></p>
<h3>Talent Mobility Networks and a Comparative Study of Biomedical Innovation in China and the United States</h3>

Role: Second author.

This study compares biomedical innovation systems in China and the United States through the lens of top-scientist mobility networks, linking talent flows with innovation input, innovation output, research collaboration, and innovation transformation.
:::
:::

:::

## Master's Thesis

::: {.output-list .editorial-list}
::: {.output-item}
<h3>全球生物医药顶尖科学家城际流动网络——基于全域与自我网络双重视角</h3>

Master's thesis, 2026.

The thesis reconstructs a longitudinal view of intercity mobility among elite biomedical scientists and combines whole-network and ego-network perspectives to analyze mobility structure and formation mechanisms.
